# 0.6.1 beta 4 — Prepare for arrival and keep outdoor labels together

- Keep the low-outdoor-temperature label and its measurement beside each other
  instead of stretching the warning chip across the row. Preserve complete
  values, bounded text, the compact two-row layout and extra-information access.
- Add **Prepare for arrival** to the card and the native **Home Environment**
  device. While the home is confirmed Away, eligible automatic/PID controllers
  temporarily use the room's Home targets. Controllers with existing native
  ON/OFF permission can also prepare rooms while they are still unoccupied.
  Actual presence sensors remain unchanged.
- Add a native timeout control, defaulting to **60 minutes** and adjustable from
  **1 minute to 24 hours**. Show the remaining time and cancellation in the card.
  A repeated native Prepare press renews the deadline using the current setting.
- End preparation on arrival, cancellation or timeout. Unknown presence pauses
  its control effect without extending the deadline. Preserve the original expiry
  through a Home Assistant restart and recheck current authority before commands.
- Preserve explicit presets, Manual/Off, manual pauses, window checks, minimum
  device ON/OFF times, power limits and startup protections. Preparation follows
  actual demand; it does not unconditionally switch on every device.
- Keep original presence gates for legacy and setpoint-only controls that cannot
  safely end an occupied-room override. Monitor every configured household
  tracker so arrival is detected even if its old room controller is disabled,
  and use the same household presence for the button and device controllers.
- Restore an already-running native thermostat's current profile setpoint when
  the room is within that profile's temperature range. This prevents an expired
  preparation target from remaining active without changing its HVAC mode.
- Add native control names in all 38 supported locales and purpose-specific
  English, Greek and German help, plus lifecycle, command and browser regressions.

Install the new beta, restart Home Assistant, and refresh the dashboard to load
the updated card and new native controls. No existing settings are reset.
Existing releases, assets and tags are retained.
